title: Sunny and the Butterfly | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka finds a butterfly resting with its wings closed on a moonlit leaf — completely still and folded, looking like a small piece of the leaf itself — and realises that even the most brilliant things need to rest. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The butterfly was resting.

Sunny almost didn't see it at first — it was sitting with its wings folded tight, and from the side it looked exactly like a small dried leaf standing up on the larger leaf beneath it. Only when she crept very close did she see the tiny body, the furled antennae, the curved edge that was wing and not leaf.

She breathed very carefully.

With its wings closed, she could see the underside — pale grey-brown, patterned with eye-spots and tracings that looked like bark, like lichen, like everything it was trying not to be found among. Perfect camouflage.

She thought: all day it was colour. All day it was wing-spread and sun-catching and movement. And now it is stillness.

The butterfly did not move.

She imagined it open — the wings she couldn't see, folded away inside. Whatever brilliant pattern was inside there, hidden from the night, waiting for morning.

She thought: some things save their best for the right moment.

She sat down beside the leaf.

The butterfly slept on, folded and still and perfectly itself.

She watched over it for a while.

Then she closed her eyes.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, butterfly. Goodnight, little one.
